items.summary: Cyient Semiconductors secured a $10 million strategic equity investment from US-based chipmaker GlobalFoundries, valuing the Hyderabad-headquartered company at $510 million post-money.The investment will be made at a pre-money equity valuation of $490 million, the same valuation as Cyient Semiconductors' recent funding round led by Edelweiss, the company said in a regulatory filing on Thursday.The fresh investment is aimed at expanding Cyient Semiconductors' turnkey custom application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) capabilities, accelerating custom silicon development and strengthening long-term wafer supply assurance and supply chain resilience.The partnership is expected to improve the company's access to advanced manufacturing capabilities and support its efforts to scale engineering operations and global customer engagements."This investment is a strong validation of our vision and the opportunity ahead for semiconductor innovation from India," said Suman Narayan, CEO of Cyient Semiconductors, adding that the investment would help the company strengthen its engineering capabilities, accelerate innovation and expand its global customer engagements.Cyient is focused on delivering custom silicon solutions to customers across automotive, industrial, AI, communications, and data center markets.

Tata Technologies Ltd, which provides product engineering and digital services to manufacturers, aims to double its revenue to USD 1.1-1.3 billion while expanding operating profit margin to more than 20 per cent by 2030.
The company is betting on multiple large full-vehicle projects, software services and the aerospace and industrial heavy machinery segment. Its  revenue in FY26 was around USD 600 million with an EBITDA margin of 15.5 per cent.
The company is expecting revenue to grow in double digits in current financial year FY27 and to expand further at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15-20 per cent between FY27 and FY30, according to an investor presentation.
Tata Technologies provides product engineering and digital services to manufacturers. The company primarily serves the automotive sector while it is expanding in the aerospace and industrial heavy machinery spaces.
Its services include the product lifecycle, from designing and developing vehicles and other products

items.summary:
Realty firm Puravankara Ltd will invest around Rs 800 crore over the next four years in the construction of a premium housing project here, as part of its expansion plan, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
The company has launched a new housing project, 'Purva Cityspire', which is part of its 18-acre township, Purva City, at Edappally in Kochi.
"We are launching a new project in our 18-acre township. The total apartments will be 1,056," said Mallanna Sasalu, CEO-South, Puravankara.
When asked about the project cost, he said the company already owns the land.
"The investment on pure construction will be around Rs 800 crore," he told PTI.
The estimated revenue potential from this upcoming project is about Rs 2,000 crore, Sasalu said.
Homes range from 1,271 sq ft to 1,895 sq ft, with prices starting at Rs 1.44 crore.
The construction work will start soon, and the project is expected to be completed in four years.

items.summary: Shares of PVR Inox jumped around 4% on Wednesday, extending gains to over 6% in two days after ratings agency CRISIL revised its outlook for the firm’s long-term bank facilities and non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to ‘Positive’ from ‘Stable’.PVR Inox shares hit a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on NSE today, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. Along with the outlook upgrade, CRISIL Ratings also reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on the long term debt instruments of the company.Why did Crisil upgrade its outlook for PVR Inox?The rating on the short-term bank facilities and commercial paper programme has been reaffirmed at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency said the outlook upgrade was driven by expectations of sustained growth in the company’s scale of operations across multiple revenue streams and improvement in operating margin strengthening its business risk profile. The outlook revision also accounts for the strengthening of the company’s financial risk profile by becoming a net cash company during the first half of fiscal 2027.Also read | District's PVR INOX ticket sales jump 60%, rivals lag at 4%The structural improvement is driven by PVR Inox’s ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, thereby reducing content concentration risk, Crisil said. It added that the content ecosystem has become increasingly diversified, with admissions being supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content. The industry has also witnessed increasing success of mid-budget films which lowers the dependence on a few marquee releases and provides greater stability to admissions and occupancy.Alternate content initiatives such as re-releases, concert screenings, anime content and sports broadcasts have also emerged as supplementary demand drivers and improve utilisation of the existing screen network, Crisil said. It noted that the concerns around OTT-led disruption have also moderated as the theatrical-first release model has been re-established, with producers increasingly using theatrical performance as the primary benchmark for content monetisation on OTT, highlighting the complementary nature of theatrical and digital channels.PVR Inox’s business risk profile is also supported by increasing geographical diversification as the company continues to expand its presence in southern India and tier 2 and 3 markets, which benefit from strong movie-going culture, multiple thriving film industries and relatively low multiplex penetration, the ratings agency said, further noting that the company’s screen portfolio in southern markets increased from 31% at the end of fiscal 2023 to 34% in at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, with more than 35% of screen additions over the past three years originating from the region. “This diversification supports admissions visibility and reduces dependence on any single language or regional content cycle,” it said.Crisil further highlighted PVR Inox’s earnings, pointing out that the company demonstrated healthy revenue growth driven by a mix of increasing admissions, increasing average ticket prices (ATP), higher spends per head (SPH), and improving monetisation of its customer base. Net debt reduced, aided by strong accrual generation and proceeds from the divestment of the 4700 BC business for about Rs 227 crore in January 2026. Despite completion of a Rs 300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027, leverage metrics are expected to remain comfortable, the ratings agency said. It expects the company’s net worth to remain healthy and gradually improve over the medium term, supported by strong accrual.“The ratings reflect the company’s strong market position with an established brand, expectation of further improvement in operating efficiency, led by synergistic benefits and premiumisation, and a strong financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility of the film exhibition business with operating performance remaining dependent on the quality and timing of content releases and evolving consumer preferences,” it said.Also read | PVR INOX bets on smaller multiplexes as single-screens declinePVR Inox share pricePVR Inox shares jumped more than 9% in a week and 23% in a month. This comes amid blockbuster releases including Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Part 1. The stock has so far gained more than 70% in 2026.The shares of the multiplex chain operator have delivered 55% returns over one year. In the longer term, the stock gained more than 4.5% in three years and 2% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 16,896 crore.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. AI may cut drug development time, says Biocon's Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
items.summary:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to drastically cut the time required to take a drug molecule from the lab to patients, compressing the current five-to-seven-year timeline into just one or two years, Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw of Biocon said on Tuesday.
Speaking on the role of AI in life sciences, Shaw, the Executive Chairperson, Biocon Ltd, noted that accelerating this journey from lab to clinic will unlock major opportunities in precision and personalised medicine.
"Ultimately the process of drug development doesn't end in the labs. It has to be validated in clinical trials. How do you pick the right patients? How do you conduct these trials in a way that gives you early readouts?
"This is all what AI is going to be used for in the future. So today it takes you almost five to seven years to get a molecule from lab all the way to the patients. Can we compress that into a year or two? That is going to be the most fascinating outcome and impact," she said on the first day of t
